claim: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) affects 5–18% of women in reproductive age worldwide.
source: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is the single most common endocrine-metabolic disorder affecting 5–18% of women in reproductive age worldwide (Joham et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Joham et al., 2022.

claim: PCOS is diagnosed based on the criteria of hyperandrogenism, oligo-anovulation, and polycystic ovarian morphology (PCOM).
source: As a multifactorial disorder with no clearly defined etiology, PCOS is diagnosed based on the criteria of hyperandrogenism, oligo-anovulation, and polycystic ovarian morphology (PCOM) (Joham et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Joham et al., 2022.

claim: PCOS is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation and potential autoimmune sequelae.
source: The syndrome is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation and potential autoimmune sequelae (Gaberšček et al., 2015), further aggravated by obesity.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gaberšček et al., 2015.

claim: Women affected with PCOS are at increased risk for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D).
source: Indeed, women affected with PCOS are at increased risk for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) (Azziz, 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Azziz, 2018.

claim: Women with PCOS have a higher prevalence of autoimmune thyroid disease (AITD), particularly hypothyroidism.
source: with a number of studies indicating also a higher prevalence of autoimmune thyroid disease (AITD), and particularly hypothyroidism (Gaberšček et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gaberšček et al., 2015.

claim: Serological parameters of autoimmunity, such as anti-histone and anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies, are relatively high among women with PCOS.
source: In support of this observation, serological parameters of autoimmunity, such as anti-histone and anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies, are relatively high among these women (Hefler-Frischmuth et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hefler-Frischmuth et al., 2010.

claim: Attempts to identify an autoimmune cause of PCOS have been uninformative.
source: However, attempts to identify an autoimmune cause of PCOS have been uninformative (Gleicher, 1998; Mobeen et al., 2016; Petríková et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gleicher, 1998; Mobeen et al., 2016; Petríková et al., 2010.

claim: Hyperandrogenemia is a hallmark feature of PCOS that plays a key role in the pathophysiology and seems to be directly related to disease severity.
source: Hyperandrogenemia is a hallmark feature of PCOS that plays a key role in the pathophysiology and seems to be directly related to disease severity (Joham et al., 2022; Diamanti-Kandarakis and Dunaif, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Joham et al., 2022; Diamanti-Kandarakis and Dunaif, 2012.

claim: It remains unknown whether the observed immune responses and autoimmune alterations in women with PCOS are a cause or consequence of hyperandrogenemia.

evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hu et al., 2020.

claim: B cells exacerbate metabolic disease in the pathogenesis of diabetes.

evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Deng et al., 2016.

claim: B cells exacerbate metabolic disease in obesity-associated insulin resistance.

claim: Mu heavy chain knockout mice (MuMt-; Bnull) fail to produce mature B cells.
